desks.Dividends: The only confirmed ex-date in the next four weeks is Nvidia, Dec 2, $0.25 per quarter at the unchanged rate, payable Dec 23 — a routine payment at a sub-1% yield with no capture angle. SPY's Dec 18 distribution is on the issuer's published schedule but still undeclared; QQQ's Dec 21 amount is disputed across third-party sources and is UNVERIFIED. Microsoft went ex Nov 19 at the raised $0.98, its 24th consecutive annual increase, first payment Dec 10. Apple last went ex Nov 12 at $0.27; Tesla pays no dividend.
desks.Earnings: No watchlist name reports earnings in the next two weeks (Nov 23-Dec 7); the next prints cluster in late January 2027 (Microsoft and Tesla ~Jan 27, Apple ~Jan 28). Nvidia reported Tue Nov 17 after close — revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y), Data Center $107.6B, EPS $2.70 GAAP / $2.68 non-GAAP, Q4 guide $130B. The stock faded 2.89% on the print, then fell to $125.53 by Friday before today's rebound. No options-implied expected move is reportable for the window.
desks.Futures: WTI ~$80.27, down about 4% Monday after a weekend of Hormuz tanker strikes — the market is pricing surplus, not war. The IEA flipped its Q4 balance to a 1.7M b/d surplus, and the EIA reported a +3.38M bbl crude build vs +0.058M expected. Brent fell 3-4% on the day; its exact level is UNVERIFIED to ±$1 (sources $86.70-$88.70). Gold rebounded ~3.4% to $3,634.80 after its steepest weekly fall since March; natgas fell 6-8% on milder weather. OPEC+ meets Sun Nov 29; next EIA weekly Wed Nov 25.
desks.Parity: No parity violation was found on the watchlist. The freshest independent box-spread measurement (Nov 12 data) printed implied financing of 3.86% at the short end to 5.16% at 435 days — close to Treasury yields, not a dislocation. Cboe's AM-settled SPX weeklies under the new SPXO symbol are live since Nov 9, with the first expiries Nov 18 and Dec 16 — the same underlying now trades under three symbols, so cross-symbol parity on coincident expiries is the item to watch.
desks.Premium: Near-expiry at-the-money IV runs from SPY 22.3% to Nvidia 79.2% at 1-2 DTE, on a day when the tape rallied sharply — but no clean rich/cheap premium verdict is available. Every 20-day realized window is WINDOW-CONTINGENT: the Nov 5 crash day drives more than 30% of realized variance for all six names, and Nvidia's window is now dominated by its Nov 20 -15.1% day. IV rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names. No watchlist earnings within the IV window; the front of the curve is flat to mildly front-elevated, with Nvidia the only large front premium (+15.6pp).
desks.Quant lab: Eleven new candidates ledgered (#328-338), run max 59, nothing TEST- or INTEGRATE-ready. Top score #331 VerifiQuant (59, WATCH): governance-by-execution for financial LLM workflows, fail-closed numeric gating that matches desk discipline — code link stated but not verified. #338 Clark (51, WATCH) finds IV-spread return predictability depends on firm type, directly premium-desk relevant.
